solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Retirement of very good host aroused critical comment

indicators.note: retirement is a drawing back, so the word for very good is read backwards

parts.note: tip-top: top means very good

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so the letters of host are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A host who has stepped down is stirred into making a cutting remark about someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' looks like leaving a job, but here it means drawing back, so the word reads in reverse; 'aroused' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A potshot is a casual, often unfair, swipe of criticism aimed at a target.

clue.text: Routine cop with cap devised — an obsessive tendency?

indicators.note: devised means worked out afresh, so these letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A policeman's routine with his hat suggests he is obsessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A preoccupation is a fixation that fills the mind.

clue.text: Young child on road in city characterising a symbol?

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: in means the road goes inside the city letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
M1 is a British motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A toddler on a street in a city typifies something.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London's postcode; MI stands for the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Totemic means relating to a totem, an emblem standing for a group.

clue.text: Tennis player with no end of aggression, virile type

indicators.note: with no means the following letter is taken out

parts.note: Tim Henman was a leading British tennis player

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of aggression

explanation.surface: A tennis star lacking killer instinct is still a macho man.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Henman was a famous British tennis player of the 1990s and 2000s; remove N, the last letter of 'aggression'.
explanation.definitionFit: A he-man is a strong, muscular, masculine fellow.

clue.text: Sun seen around old muddy place good for wintry transport

indicators.note: around means the sun word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: sun as a verb means to tan, as in sunbathing
a bog is a wet, muddy place

explanation.surface: Sunshine over an old swamp makes a good spot for winter travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a sled ridden down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Secretary right to enter filthy place for food

parts.note: PA, a personal assistant, is a secretary

indicators.note: to enter means the letter for right goes inside the word for a filthy place

parts.note: a sty, where pigs live, is a byword for a filthy place

explanation.surface: A secretary walks into a squalid spot looking for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry is baked dough, a kind of edible fare.

clue.text: Local look about European settlement abroad

indicators.note: about means the pub word goes round the European letter

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone at their regular bar looks over a European town overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British term for one's neighbourhood pub; LO is an old word for 'look!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pueblo is a village or town, especially in Spanish-speaking lands or the US Southwest.

clue.text: Piece held by sister behind medical transplantation

indicators.note: held by means the chess word sits inside the sister abbreviation

parts.note: the king is a chess piece
aft means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A nurse holds a fragment behind her during a surgical transfer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin graft moves healthy tissue to cover a wound, a surgical transfer.

clue.text: Cotton on island featured in genuine exports originally

indicators.note: featured in means the island letters appear inside the other pieces

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of exports

explanation.surface: Cotton grown on an island appears among real exports at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton on' is the phrasal verb meaning understand, not the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is informal for coming to understand, to grasp.

clue.text: Praiseworthy site moved chap touring Britain

indicators.note: moved signals that the letters of site shift into another order
touring means going around, so the word for chap wraps the letter for Britain

parts.note: a chap is a male

explanation.surface: A fellow travelling around Britain finds a relocated site worthy of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' is the anagram signal for 'site'; 'touring' means the chap goes round Britain's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something estimable deserves esteem, so it is worthy of admiration.

clue.text: Vacuous way in which game ends?

parts.note: the written word game ends with an E, read here as the letters of 'an E'

explanation.surface: A dull, empty way for a match to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is not a match but the written word, whose final letter is E: the way it ends is 'in an E'. 'way' and 'which' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and empty of meaning, just as vacuous does.

clue.text: List of cross suppliers?

parts.note: voters mark a cross on their ballot paper, so a register of voters lists those who supply crosses

explanation.definitionFit: The electoral roll is the official register of people entitled to vote.

clue.text: For starters, chef uses many ingredients normally as flavour

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so take the first letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A chef usually uses lots of ingredients to add flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumin is a spice used to give dishes taste.

clue.text: Explosive stuff found on reflection in meeting I legitimised

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: After some thought, a meeting that I approved turns up some explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ETINGILEG sits inside 'meeting I legitimised'; 'on reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is a blasting material used in quarrying and demolition.

clue.text: A French meal's cooked around college in America

indicators.note: around means the other letters wrap round the abbreviation for college

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: cooked signals that the letters of meal's are reworked

explanation.surface: A French dinner is prepared around a college in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' is the anagram signal for 'meal's'; 'around' has the French article plus that anagram wrap the college letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the personification of the United States government and nation.

clue.text: Half of pop group enclosed by barrier lacking fine lasting quality

indicators.note: enclosed by means the pop letters sit inside the shortened barrier
lacking means the letter for fine is dropped

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
F is an abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: half of means only the first of the two identical halves of the band name is kept

parts.note: Duran Duran was a 1980s British pop band whose name repeats one word

explanation.surface: Half a pop band is fenced in, with no fine staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: Duran Duran was a 1980s British pop group; FENCE without F is ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is staying power, the capacity to last.

clue.text: A learner in part of camp showing ability

indicators.note: in means the a and the learner letter go inside the camp shelter

parts.note: a tent is one unit of a campsite
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee at a campsite shows real skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent is a natural gift or aptitude.

clue.text: Language declined around society with restricted observance

indicators.note: around means the declined word wraps the society letter

parts.note: sank means declined or fell

indicators.note: restricted means the ritual word is cut short

parts.note: a rite is a religious observance

explanation.surface: A tongue fell out of use around a society with limited rituals.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the ancient classical tongue of India.

clue.text: Information kept by a lawyer in plan for meeting

indicators.note: kept by means the word for information is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: DA, district attorney, is a US lawyer
gen is informal British for information

explanation.surface: A lawyer holds on to the facts in preparation for a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda lists the items to be discussed at a gathering.

clue.text: Companion among small number with general held up — group at a level?

indicators.note: among means the companion letters go inside the others
held up in a down clue means read upward, backwards

parts.note: no is short for number
Robert E. Lee was a Confederate general
CH is Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A companion among a few is held up with a general in a group of equals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns NO + LEE to EELON; CH goes 'among' to give E-CH-ELON.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a rank or tier in an organisation.

clue.text: Titled figure with English bishop entertaining earl as figure in exchange?

parts.note: Bart is short for baronet, a titled man

indicators.note: entertaining means holding, so the bishop letters hold the earl letter

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the style of a bishop

explanation.surface: A baronet and an English bishop host an earl at some trading occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: BART is the abbreviation for baronet; RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: One who barters swaps goods rather than paying money, a participant in trade.

clue.text: Excellent drink promoted in ceremonial privileges?

indicators.note: promoted means raised up, so in a down clue the pieces read upward

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI
lager is a drink

explanation.surface: A top-quality drink served at a ceremony befitting royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' reverses AILAGER; A1 is written with I for the numeral 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems and rights of royalty or office.

clue.text: Locate below sides of dome oppressive sort

indicators.note: below in a down clue puts the locating word under the dome letters
sides of means the first and last letters of dome

parts.note: to spot is to locate

explanation.surface: Find something beneath the edges of a dome, a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a tyrant ruling with absolute power.

clue.text: Working together like a sound parachutist?

definitions.meaning: a team pulling jointly, as horses yoked side by side
a safe skydiver is properly strapped into the webbing that holds the chute

explanation.definitionFit: Draught horses in harness pull together, hence cooperating; a parachutist is safely buckled into the straps.

clue.text: Magnate has way of working by bay largely

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of working

indicators.note: largely means most of the word for bay is used, its tail cut

parts.note: a gulf is a large bay

explanation.surface: A tycoon has a method of operating near the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful business figure, a tycoon.

clue.text: Secretive group with revolutionary intention to seize a fellow

indicators.note: to seize means the reversed word grabs the following letters inside
revolutionary means turned round, so the intention word is reversed

parts.note: aim means intention

explanation.surface: A clandestine band plans revolution and grabs a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns AIM to MIA, which seizes A and F.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is a secret criminal organisation.

clue.text: Material carried by many Londoners

indicators.note: carried by means the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Fabric toted about by many people in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric.

clue.text: Top floor I mismanaged — area of minister's responsibility?

indicators.note: mismanaged means badly handled, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A government minister confesses to running the top floor badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's portfolio is the government department or brief they hold.

clue.text: Buy property, say, with minimal coverage?

definitions.meaning: to put money into an asset such as a house
wearing only an undershirt, scarcely dressed

explanation.definitionFit: To put money into assets for return; split, someone in a vest is barely clothed.

clue.text: Hard work very advanced in short advertisement

indicators.note: in means the two short letters go inside the shortened promotion
short means the advertisement word loses its ending

parts.note: a trailer is an advertisement for a film

explanation.surface: Gruelling labour goes into a brief promotional spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TRAILER to TRAIL; V and A go 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful, laborious effort.
